correctness.rationale: For all n,k>=1, the color-support map is a surjective bounded morphism of full nonzero co-consistency frames; its back condition is witnessed by a current-state atom in a requested color and representatives of remaining requested colors. It preserves p_i since atomic forcing means A is contained in B_i. The formula delta_t = conjunction of positive p_i for 1-bits and negated Diamond p_i for 0-bits characterizes exactly monochromatic states. Diamond delta_t detects colors in the pointed state and Diamond Diamond delta_t detects colors anywhere in the full frame using the universal state as intermediate successor. These prove profile iff, count by nonempty S subset T, stage equivalence if n>=2^k and strictness otherwise by the depth-three Psi_Q. All boundary quantifiers are explicit. An independent direct finite evaluator tested 315460 formula-world comparisons, 10466 stage-separator instances and 8434 pointed color-profile instances. No finite test substitutes for the general proof.

value.rationale: The source introduces a natural modal language with constrained Boolean-valued atomic translations; the question of exactly which finite Boolean atoms the language can distinguish is intrinsic to that semantics. The theorem gives a complete modal-theory classification for all full finite frames, an exact naturally indexed theory count and saturation, and optimal variable resources for distinguishing finite stages with explicit bounded-depth separators.
